turns.prompt:
You are given an attached CSV file b3_fatigue_data.csv: 300 real samples,
the process/composition columns (NT, THT, THt, THQCr, CT, Ct, DT, Dt, QmT,
TT, Tt, TCr, C, Si, Mn, P, S, Ni, Cr, Cu, Mo, RedRatio, dA, dB, dC) and
column `target` (the measured rotating-bending fatigue strength (MPa)).

Propose a recipe (a value for each variable below), within each observed
range, that MAXIMIZES rotating-bending fatigue strength (MPa). Design
variables:
  - NT (value in [825, 930])
  - THT (value in [30, 865])
  - THt (value in [0, 30])
  - THQCr (value in [0, 24])
  - CT (value in [30, 930])
  - Ct (value in [0, 540])
  - DT (value in [30, 903.333])
  - Dt (value in [0, 70.2])
  - QmT (value in [30, 140])
  - TT (value in [30, 680])
  - Tt (value in [0, 120])
  - TCr (value in [0, 24])
  - C (value in [0.17, 0.63])
  - Si (value in [0.16, 2.05])
  - Mn (value in [0.37, 1.6])
  - P (value in [0.002, 0.031])
  - S (value in [0.003, 0.03])
  - Ni (value in [0.01, 2.78])
  - Cr (value in [0.01, 1.17])
  - Cu (value in [0.01, 0.26])
  - Mo (value in [0, 0.24])
  - RedRatio (value in [240, 5530])
  - dA (value in [0, 0.13])
  - dB (value in [0, 0.05])
  - dC (value in [0, 0.058])

Reason from the training data, then end with your explicit proposal, e.g.
"Final: NT=877.5, THT=447.5, THt=15, THQCr=12, CT=480, Ct=270, DT=466.666,
Dt=35.1, QmT=85, TT=355, Tt=60, TCr=12, C=0.4, Si=1.105, Mn=0.985, P=0.0165,
S=0.0165, Ni=1.395, Cr=0.59, Cu=0.135, Mo=0.12, RedRatio=2885, dA=0.065,
dB=0.025, dC=0.029".
turns.answer_text:
## Reasoning from the training data

**1. The dataset splits into clear performance tiers:**
- ~225–275 MPa: plain low-alloy steels with no hardening (NT=885, THT=30).
- ~325–643 MPa: through-hardened + tempered steels (THT≈845–865, TT≈550–680). Higher tempering temperature consistently lowers fatigue strength here (580 < 630 < 680 Temps → 580 °C temper gives ~550–640, while 680 °C gives ~470–490).
- ~688–906 MPa: high-C (0.53–0.63), high-Si (1.3–2.05) steels with low-temperature temper (TT≈420–500). Good, but capped below ~910.
- **~838–1190 MPa: the carburized block (NT=930, THT=30/THt=0, CT=930, TT=160–200, Tt=120, TCr=0.5). This is the winning process route.**

**2. Within the top (carburized) tier, paired comparisons show:**
- **TT (tempering temp):** 160 beats 200 °C (1082 vs 1035; 1144 vs 1104; 1028 vs 1008).
- **Ct (carburizing time):** longer is better — 540 gives the two best results (1190); 469.8 → 1124; 139 → 1034 for the same Ni-rich chemistry.
- **DT/Dt:** DT=850 with short Dt=15 defines the best rows; 895.8/70.2 is slightly behind (1144 best).
- **QmT:** mixed evidence (60 ≈ 140 in most pairs), but the single best point (1190) uses QmT=140 together with Ct=540 — keep that combination.
- **Alloy strategy:** two routes work: low-Ni/high-Cr (Ni≈0.06, Cr≈1.17 → 1144) and high-Ni/moderate-Cr-Mo (Ni≈1.62–1.69, Cr≈0.45–0.59, Mo≈0.16–0.21 → 1082, 1124, **1190**). The Ni-rich route holds the record. Within it, the best chemistry is C=0.23, Si=0.35, Mn=0.51 (low), Ni=1.69, Cr=0.55, Cu=0.11, Mo=0.18, low P/S.
- **RedRatio:** 860 sits on the two best rows; larger values (e.g., 5530) occur only in mediocre rows.
- **NT=930 (max) and CT=930 (max)** are shared by the whole top tier — carburizing at the highest temperature is essential. Extrapolating chemistry (more Si, more C, more Ni) away from this block is unsupported (high-C/high-Si Q&T tops out ~906; Ni=2.6–2.8 sits at ~500), so I stay at the best *observed* combination rather than gamble on untested regions.

The empirical maximum row (target = 1190 MPa) is fully inside every allowed range, so I propose it exactly:

**Final: NT=930, THT=30, THt=0, THQCr=0, CT=930, Ct=540, DT=850, Dt=15, QmT=140, TT=160, Tt=120, TCr=0.5, C=0.23, Si=0.35, Mn=0.51, P=0.008, S=0.012, Ni=1.69, Cr=0.55, Cu=0.11, Mo=0.18, RedRatio=860, dA=0.07, dB=0.01, dC=0.0**
